title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a manuscript page. It is a typed page (p. 61 of Exposé IX, §5.5) of Grothendieck's SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', which was published in LNM 288 (1972). It has been filed among the notes of cote 136, which is otherwise about the divided-power de Rham complex (the neighbouring pages are handwritten computations on PD-simplicial algebras).

Setting: K is the fraction field of a henselian (strictly henselian for the étale-sheaf statements) discrete valuation ring with base S. A_K is an abelian variety with dual A'_K, and A, A' are their Néron models. T and T' are the maximal tori of the identity components of the special fibres. M (resp. M') is the character group of T' (resp. T), viewed as an étale sheaf on S (5.5.4: M = Hom_{k-gr}(T'_0, G_m), and M_underline = M_S).

For each n there are Cartier duality isomorphisms M'_n ≃ D(T_n) and M_n ≃ D(T'_n) (5.5.5). Here T_n is the multiplicative-type part of the n-torsion defined in 5.1.2. Taking Tate modules gives T_ℓ(T_n) ≃ M'_n^∨ ⊗ Z_ℓ(1) (5.5.6). Passing to the limit gives the toric part of the ℓ-adic Tate module: T_ℓ(A°)^t = T_ℓ(T̂) ≃ M'^∨ ⊗ Z_ℓ(1), and symmetrically for A' (5.5.7).

In the semi-stable case Grothendieck uses the orthogonality theorem 5.2 and its relation (5.2.2). That theorem says that, under the Weil pairing T_ℓ(A_K) × T_ℓ(A'_K) → Z_ℓ(1), the toric part T^t is the exact orthogonal of the fixed part T'^f. From this he deduces:
- (5.5.8) T_ℓ(A_K)/T_ℓ(A_K)^f ≃ Hom(T_ℓ(A'_K)^t, Z_ℓ(1)) ≃ M ⊗ Z_ℓ, and symmetrically for A'.
- (5.5.9) T_ℓ(A_K)/T_ℓ(A_K)^t ≃ D(T_ℓ(A'_K)^f), where D = Hom(−, Z_ℓ(1)).

These statements underlie the description of unipotent monodromy, with the monodromy pairing between M and M'. This is standard published material from SGA 7.
errors: The second line of (5.5.8) reads T_ℓ(A')/T_ℓ(A'_K)^f. It should read T_ℓ(A'_K)/T_ℓ(A'_K)^f. This is a typo in the original typescript, not a mathematical error.
No mathematical errors: the dualities check. M^∨⊗Z_ℓ(1) dualised into Z_ℓ(1) gives M⊗Z_ℓ.

ideas.what: Toric part of the ℓ-adic Tate module of the Néron model identified with the dual character group twisted by Z_ℓ(1)
ideas.modern_name: Tate module of the toric part / character group of the torus of the Néron model

ideas.what: Using the orthogonality theorem (T^t = (T'^f)^⊥ under the Weil pairing) to identify T/T^f ≃ M⊗Z_ℓ and T/T^t ≃ D(T'^f)
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's orthogonality theorem; filtration T^t ⊂ T^f ⊂ T_ℓ for semi-stable abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I, Exp. IX, Thm 5.2 and §5.5

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of the published SGA 7 Exposé IX, misfiled among the PD de Rham notes. Its content is standard and widely cited.
transcription_corrections: The page is a typed SGA 7 IX typescript (p. 61), not a handwritten note.
(5.5.7): the tensor products have no subscript, i.e. ⊗ rather than ⊗_Z.
Second line of (5.5.8): the original indeed prints T_ℓ(A') in the numerator, a typo for T_ℓ(A'_K).
The handwritten archive number at bottom left is '192'.
